# Fingerling (01, engineer) — BAD-008

## Brief
Make collab create atomic in BadTakes, so a failure after the room is minted can never leave an open, unreachable room behind, and confirm or close the second orphan path from the 2026-08-26 incident.

Background (ticket BAD-008, from BadTakes TODO.md item 43): private.create_collab inserts and commits the collab row; server/supabase/functions/collab/index.ts then stamps visibility, character_count and scene_cast in a separate UPDATE ("Stamped after the fact", near line 391). When that UPDATE throws, the room survives and the caller gets an error. In production ten such failures filled every MAX_OPEN_COLLABS slot, and each orphan holds collabs_one_hosted_per_scene, so the scene answers already_hosting for 24h (sweepExpired's IDLE_TTL_MS). main.js writes the scene.json pin only after collab:create returns ok, so an orphan is unreachable from the desktop.

Work, in this order:
1. Atomic create. Move the three stamps inside create_collab's transaction (widen its signature in a NEW migration; never edit an applied one), so a stamping failure rolls the room back. Read migration 0026's note on why they were kept out (a row lock on the licence while it decides the paid check and the open-collab cap) and keep that locking correct. Update the collab function to call the widened function and drop the after-the-fact UPDATE. If atomicity is genuinely unsafe, fall back to closing the just-minted room when the stamp throws (as uploadSceneForCollab already does for an upload failure) and say why.
2. Integration test in test/server/ proving a failing stamp leaves no open room and no already_hosting lock (and that the normal create still stamps all three columns).
3. Reconcile. Check whether an orphan shows in the collab endpoint's 'mine' mode and in web/collabweb.js renderMyCollabs (it filters to active or wrapped phases). If an unpinned open room is invisible, make it visible and cancellable host-side, on web and on the desktop. If the desktop part grows past a small change, stop at the server and web half and file a proposal for the desktop list instead.
4. Second orphan path. Three rooms whose create and stamp both succeeded were also invisible. Trace whether a failed scene upload whose close or unpin did not land leaves an orphan; fix it if it does and it is small, otherwise file a proposal with the evidence. Report what you found either way; do not call the ticket fixed without an answer.
5. Close TODO.md item 43 per the committing-and-pushing skill (condense in TODO.md, full write-up to TODO_DONE.md), since this PR ships it.

Setup and verification (BadTakes rules win on how it is built and verified):

- Containers are podman, never Docker/OrbStack. Never `supabase login`, never a push or apply against production, never the Supabase MCP's apply_migration. Deploys happen in CI on merge.
- Prove the migration composes with the scratch Postgres recipe in server-changes (`admin/scripts/apply-migrations.mjs` against a throwaway podman Postgres), drive the widened function by hand with psql, and drop the container after.
- The local Supabase stack is shared across worktrees. Run `podman ps` first. If no supabase containers are running, you may start it from this worktree per server/README.md (DOCKER_HOST at podman's socket, `-x edge-runtime,vector,logflare`, `supabase db reset`, `functions serve` from this worktree) and run test/server/functions.test.mjs; stop what you started when done and say so. If another worktree's stack is up, do not touch it; rely on the scratch Postgres proof and say the Server integration CI check is the remaining proof.
- `npm test` must pass; say which suites ran and which skipped.
- If you touch main.js, preload.js or renderer/, run the scoped smoke (`BT_LIBRARY_ROOT` at a copy of fixtures/library) and inspect the screenshots.
- Never JSON.stringify a value into a sql`` template; use sql.json.
